# Fungi

> *How do fungi differ from bacteria, and why does being eukaryotic make them harder to target?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Eukaryotic microbes that grow as yeasts, moulds, or switch between the two with temperature.

**How members differ (the sorting key):** Yeast, mould or dimorphic; ergosterol versus cholesterol; who gets infected (host factors).

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** *Candida albicans* (commensal turned opportunist), *Aspergillus* (inhaled spores), *Cryptococcus* (capsule).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** Dermatophytes, *Histoplasma*, *Pneumocystis*.

**Later in the course:** Skin, lung and opportunistic infections in the organ blocks; antifungal drugs in pharmacology.
